method: Current primary and authoritative sources only. Employer postings establish title usage and repeated responsibilities; official engineering documentation, protocol specifications, and public-sector material establish current implementation concerns. Recruiting artifacts and vendor guidance are not treated as universal standards.

sources.title: Agentic AI Engineer
sources.evidence_summary: Uses the exact title in banking and requires Python, microservices/APIs, distributed cloud systems, multi-agent orchestration, production readiness, observability, and collaboration with product/domain roles.
sources.limitations: ING notes its global job architecture may label the position Engineer III or IV; one new squad and a GenAI-heavy implementation context.

sources.title: Agentic AI Engineer
sources.evidence_summary: Defines end-to-end ownership from problem framing and architecture through evaluation, deployment, incidents, and iteration, with planner/worker and multi-agent patterns, tool routing, state management, error handling, human checkpoints, MCP integration, regression tests, tracing, and feedback loops.
sources.limitations: One industrial-energy employer with an Azure/Databricks/Snowflake implementation stack; title and tool list are not universal.

sources.title: Principal Agentic AI Engineer
sources.evidence_summary: Uses the exact principal title and combines hands-on end-to-end production delivery with standardized action interfaces, deterministic decision-grade results, evaluation, reliability/safety patterns, observability, performance/cost tradeoffs, and technical leadership.
sources.limitations: Principal-level platform role focused on geospatial and edge environments; broader than a typical product-agent position.

sources.title: Agentic AI Engineer (Azure Agent Framework)
sources.evidence_summary: Uses the exact title and requires multi-agent architecture, backend services, data/API integration, scalable and secure application design, testing, performance, reliability, maintainability, and CI/CD.
sources.limitations: Consulting role is tightly coupled to Microsoft/Azure products and inconsistently says architect in body text; evidence supports work pattern more strongly than standardized naming.

sources.title: Lead Agentic AI Engineer
sources.evidence_summary: The official posting describes production agent systems with tool use, planning, memory management, workflow automation, multi-agent collaboration, backend/data integration, and MCP/A2A interoperability.
sources.limitations: Consulting role and cloud-product references can blend architecture, implementation, and client delivery; page is Workday-hosted and verification used the official indexed record.

sources.title: Agentic AI Engineer
sources.evidence_summary: Uses the exact title for a founding senior individual contributor expected to own technical direction, architecture, planning, and delivery of an agentic AI portfolio.
sources.limitations: Founding role can be unusually broad; full dynamic page was not extractable, so only official indexed content supports claims.

sources.title: Sr Agentic AI Solutions Engineer
sources.evidence_summary: Close title requires hands-on agent orchestration, task decomposition, multi-agent coordination, context management, performance, cost, security, and working customer reference implementations across heterogeneous infrastructure.
sources.limitations: A solutions/performance role with strong customer and hardware-platform ownership; supports adjacency and recurring technical depth, not the narrow canonical boundary by itself.

sources.title: AI Software Engineer — Agentic AI System
sources.role: AI Software Engineer — Agentic AI System
sources.evidence_summary: Close title centers hands-on infrastructure and tooling for agent evaluation, deployment/orchestration, data pipelines, dashboards, observability, and framework/model-serving integration.
sources.limitations: Infrastructure/evaluation-oriented entry role rather than full product-agent ownership; indexed official Workday record.

sources.title: Engineer 3, Agentic AI
sources.evidence_summary: Close title asks engineers to build and operate reusable agents, human/agent and agent/agent orchestration, evaluation, reliability, scalability, observability, AgentOps/MLOps contribution, and responsible use.
sources.limitations: Broad software role mixes AI-augmented SDLC and customer-facing agent products; official indexed Workday record.

sources.title: A practical guide to building agents
sources.evidence_summary: Distinguishes agents from simple LLM applications through model-managed workflow execution and tools, recommends incremental complexity, defines exit conditions and human intervention, and describes single/multi-agent orchestration and layered guardrails.
sources.limitations: Vendor guide based on customer experience and OpenAI abstractions; not a neutral standard or complete security architecture.

sources.title: Building effective agents
sources.evidence_summary: Distinguishes predefined workflows from model-directed agents, recommends simple composable patterns, emphasizes tool-interface design, environmental feedback, stopping conditions, human checkpoints, and error recovery.
sources.limitations: Anthropic notes its tooling landscape changed after publication and links to newer managed-agent material; durable patterns are stronger evidence than product details.

sources.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
sources.evidence_summary: Explains why multi-turn agents that call tools and modify state require evaluation beyond final answers, and describes combining graders and production-derived cases across an agent lifecycle.
sources.limitations: Vendor engineering experience and examples; evaluator quality remains task-specific and requires calibration.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol specification
sources.evidence_summary: Defines a standardized LLM-application connection to external data and tools and explicitly calls for consent, authorization, access controls, data protection, security, and privacy consideration.
sources.limitations: Draft/evolving protocol; the specification cannot enforce application-level security and is not a complete agent architecture.

sources.title: Understanding Authorization in MCP
sources.evidence_summary: Documents OAuth-based authorization, user-specific and administrative tool access, audit needs, scope enforcement, token validation, least privilege, secret/logging controls, and tenant/audience pitfalls.
sources.limitations: MCP HTTP authorization guidance only; local transports, enterprise IAM, effect authorization, and agent delegation need broader design.

sources.title: Announcing the Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A)
sources.evidence_summary: Describes an open protocol for agent discovery, secure information exchange, coordination, and cross-framework interoperability, positioned as complementary to MCP.
sources.limitations: Launch material and partner claims do not prove adoption, security, or fitness for a given system; implementation specifications remain versioned.

sources.title: Monitor, Evaluate, and Operate Multi-Agent AI Solutions in Azure
sources.evidence_summary: Treats distributed tracing, system-level/coordination evaluation, quality-cost-latency optimization, asynchronous human approvals, and production incident debugging as advanced multi-agent operational work.
sources.limitations: Azure product context and training-curriculum framing; supports problem categories, not a vendor-neutral design mandate.

sources.title: Accelerating the Adoption of Software and AI Agent Identity and Authorization
sources.author_or_org: NIST National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence
sources.evidence_summary: Frames agent systems as autonomous decision/action systems and identifies open engineering needs for agent identity, authentication, least privilege, delegation, intent, human binding, auditing, non-repudiation, and prompt-injection containment.
sources.limitations: Public concept paper seeking input, not a final NIST standard or normative control catalog.

sources.title: How we monitor internal coding agents for misalignment
sources.evidence_summary: Describes agent-specific risk from access to systems and safeguards, monitoring of interactions and actions, severity-based alerting, triage, mitigation, and improvement as defense in depth.
sources.limitations: Internal coding-agent context, organization-specific monitors, and reported results; not independently audited or universally transferable.

sources.title: Get started with AgentCore Observability
sources.evidence_summary: Exposes agents, sessions, detailed execution graphs, traces, spans, logs, and metrics as distinct production observability surfaces.
sources.limitations: AWS AgentCore implementation details are provider-specific; traces require privacy, retention, and semantic design beyond product setup.

sources.title: A shared playbook for trustworthy third-party evaluations
sources.evidence_summary: Argues that an agentic evaluation claim must describe the tested model, harness, tool access, safeguards, budgets, elicitation, and validity checks because these shape observed capability and risk.
sources.limitations: Frontier-model and third-party evaluation focus; principles require adaptation to product task and action-system evidence.

claims.statement: Agentic AI Engineer is a current standalone title used across multiple independent employers and industries, with close software/solutions variants supporting a broader occupation pattern.
claims.limitations: The title is emergent, not standardized, and can be hidden under generic software or AI engineering job architecture.

claims.statement: Employer evidence repeatedly expects end-to-end production engineering from problem/architecture through implementation, evaluation, deployment, operations, and iteration.
claims.limitations: Customer engagement, product ownership, and shared-platform depth vary by organization.

claims.statement: The defensible unit of accountability is acceptable task execution through bounded model-directed actions, including intermediate state, delegated authority, effects, and recovery.
claims.limitations: The boundary is a synthesis across sources rather than a standardized occupational definition.

claims.statement: Production software, API, distributed-systems, integration, testing, and deployment competence is core; agentic engineering is not prompt composition alone.
claims.limitations: Language, cloud, and framework requirements are employer-specific.

claims.statement: Agentic complexity should be justified against deterministic or fixed-workflow alternatives, and autonomy should be increased only when evidence supports it.
claims.limitations: Suitability thresholds remain task- and consequence-specific.

claims.statement: Tool and capability-interface design—including typed semantics, documentation, permissions, validation, and errors—is a first-class engineering surface.
claims.limitations: Protocol and SDK mechanisms are replaceable; effect semantics and application controls extend beyond interface descriptions.

claims.statement: Explicit state and memory management are recurring agentic responsibilities rather than incidental prompt context.
claims.limitations: Job descriptions rarely specify full provenance, retention, isolation, and conflict semantics; the deeper lifecycle is an engineering inference.

claims.statement: Multi-agent coordination is a real but optional topology whose added handoffs, state, cost, and failure paths must earn their complexity.
claims.limitations: Employer demand and protocol momentum do not prove multi-agent superiority for any given task.

claims.statement: Agent evaluation must cover task outcomes and trajectories, including tool use, state, coordination, side effects, safety, recovery, harness, and budgets—not final-answer style alone.
claims.limitations: No single grader or benchmark establishes universal agent reliability.

claims.statement: Sessions, runs, actions, traces, spans, cost, latency, and incident evidence create agent-specific observability and operational work.
claims.limitations: Telemetry content must be designed for privacy, security, cost, and diagnostic value rather than copied from a vendor dashboard.

claims.statement: Identity, authorization, least privilege, delegation, approval, revocation, and auditable action binding are central when agents access data or effectful tools.
claims.limitations: Standards and guidance are evolving; formal enterprise policy and risk decisions remain with designated specialists and owners.

claims.statement: Stopping conditions, human intervention, monitoring, and recovery are necessary controls for uncertain or consequential agent execution.
claims.limitations: Human review works only when decision rights, timing, evidence, and capacity are explicitly engineered.

claims.statement: Agent action systems create security concerns beyond output filtering, including prompt injection, confused authority, credential/tool abuse, cross-boundary data exposure, and inadequate action audit.
claims.limitations: This register validates role scope; it is not a complete threat catalog or formal security assurance.

claims.statement: MCP and A2A show current demand for standardized tool/context and agent-to-agent interoperability, but protocols are versioned implementation mechanisms rather than role identity.
claims.limitations: Protocol existence and partner participation do not prove production fitness, security, or adoption in a particular environment.

claims.statement: Current roles often skew senior because they combine AI uncertainty, distributed systems, security, production operation, and cross-functional technical judgment.
claims.limitations: Hiring years and level names are employer-specific and do not define professional competence.

claims.statement: The occupation is credible but its titles, frameworks, protocols, products, and team boundaries remain unusually volatile.
claims.limitations: Every edition needs current verification; durable concepts should dominate book architecture.

claims.statement: Recurring deliverables include action/tool and state designs, evaluation harnesses, traces, operational budgets, controls, runbooks, and change evidence rather than only agent prompts or demos.
claims.limitations: Exact artifact names are the book's synthesis; organizations distribute ownership differently.

claims.statement: The role collaborates with product, domain, data, platform, security/governance, and operational stakeholders while retaining a technical action-system accountability.
claims.limitations: Small companies and consulting engagements may combine these accountabilities in one position.
